newsitem.title: USA: Roy Weston sees positive results in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Roy Weston sees positive results in 1998.

text.p: Roy F. Weston Inc's chief executive officer said Thursday he expects the company to be producing positive results by 1998.

"While Weston faces solvable problems, we also see significant opportunities," president and chief executive officer Bill Robertson said in a press release accompanying the company's second quarter results.
"We're on the right track, and we expect that our turnaround strategy will be producing positive results by 1998," Robertson said.
For the second quarter, Weston reported a widened loss over the same period a year ago.
The company lost $5.4 million, or $0.56 per share, on revenues of $34.1 million versus a net loss a year ago of $670,000, or $0.07 per share, on revenues of $46.3 million.

Robertson said the company has streamlined management and cut its workforce by about 300 employees. Most of the reductions were associated with the May 1997 sale of the company's Environmental Metrics Division, he said.

"In addition to bolstering our core consulting and construction businesses, we've begun a process of identifying higher-margin opportunities in complementary markets where we are not currently active but our reputation and expertise would be highly valued," Robertson said.
